_comment: Frozen contract for @-mentions in message text. Three forms:
@handle   a mention: the handle is a message recipient, its herdr doorbell
rings once it is idle, and an engine handle is summoned.
@~handle  a silent mention: it names the handle (drawn as a member, found
by mentions:handle) and never wakes, addresses or summons it.
@!handle  an interrupting mention: a mention (it is in `mentions` too)
that also stops the agent mid-turn, when the sender may, so it
reads the message now. An idle agent is woken as for @handle.
A token counts only at the start of the text or after whitespace, ( or <,
so an email address is none of them.
Code is quoted, never addressed: a token inside a code span (`...`, or
``...`` and longer runs, closed by a run of the same length in the same
paragraph) or a fenced block (``` or ~~~, to its closing fence or the end
of the text) is none of them. A backtick with no matching close is a
literal backtick, not code.
@here and @all name a group, never a member called here or all, so no
handle list holds them. `groups` (an empty object when a case leaves it
out) gives each group a text names, in the strongest form it's written in:
mention, interrupt or silent (interrupt beats mention beats silent). Who a
group reaches is the hub's (fastapi-backend/app/services/groups.py).
The backend (fastapi-backend/app/services/persister.py: parse_mentions,
parse_silent_mentions, parse_interrupt_mentions), the frontend
(mycelium-frontend/src/lib/mentions.ts) and the CLI's room export
(mycelium-cli/src/mycelium/room_export.py: mentions) each parse it; all
three assert every case below: fastapi-backend/tests/test_mentions_contract.py,
mycelium-frontend/src/lib/mentions.contract.test.ts and
mycelium-cli/tests/test_mentions_contract.py.
